# Gb: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Gb** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Parted from Nut.** Born of Shu and Tefnut, Geb and Nut loved without space between them until Shu, on Ra’s command, wrenched them apart — and the world’s breathable distance dates from that separation.  Geb’s green fertility and Nut’s starry vault remain arched apart for eternity, the air god’s arms the only thing between them.

**The Five Children on the Epagomenal Days.** Though the birth of the five gods belongs to Nut’s myth, the Pyramid Texts address Geb as their father and as the mountain of the west on which the dead king ascends.  ‘You are Geb, the heir of the gods,’ the utterances tell the king — the earth is the ultimate estate of succession.

**The Tribunal of Geb.** In the New Kingdom narrative of the divine lawsuit, the gods weary of the eighty-year dispute between Horus and Seth and appeal to Geb, who as earth and eldest remaining power hears the case and awards the Two Lands to Horus, assigning Seth to the desert and the thunder — the judicial myth behind the division of the living king from the dangerous margins.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

- **Restored name:** Gb
- **ASCII form:** geb
- **Meaning:** "Earth, goose (Egyptian gb)"

- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** 𓅬
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 185 of 597

## The Name Travels

The Greeks identified Geb with their own earth — Cronos in the common equation, which made mythographic sense of his fatherhood of the divine generation.  Through Plutarch this mapping circulated widely, though Egyptian theology itself kept him younger and more fertile than the aged Titan.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Gb** stands at [/geb/](/geb/) — [lore](/geb/lore/), [scholars](/geb/scholars/), [patterns](/geb/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. The displayed form is ASCII-equivalent.
